lessons.name: What is a Computer Network?
lessons.desc: A computer network is two or more devices (computers, phones, servers, printers) connected together to share data and resources. The internet is the largest network — billions of devices all connected.
lessons.q: What is a computer network? What are the essential components that make up a network?
lessons.qsub: How do devices communicate over a network? What role do protocols play in ensuring reliable communication?
terms: Network mein ek device — computer, phone, server, router.
Do nodes ko jodne wala medium — cable, wifi, fiber.
Data ka chhota tukda jo network par bheja jata hai.
Communicate karne ke niyam — jaise HTTP, TCP.
lessons.what:
Computer network do ya zyada devices ka group hai jo data share karne ke liye aapas mein juda hota hai. Har device ko node kehte hain, aur jodne wale medium ko link.

Data ek jagah se doosri jagah chhote packets mein tut ke jata hai, aur har packet ke saath kuch rules (protocols) lagte hain jo decide karte hain ki data kaise bheja, route kiya aur milaya jata hai. Yahi puri cheez ko internet kehte hain jab millions of networks aapas mein jud jate hain.
lessons.analogy: WhatsApp group jaisa hai — har member (node) chat kar sakta hai, aur messages (packets) ek se doosre tak jate hain. Bina network ke har device ek island hai, mobile data ya wifi us island ko jodo ka pul deta hai.
lessons.why: Bina network ke aap files bhejna, messages bhejna, ya web browse nahi kar sakte. Har modern system — microservices, load balancers, databases, CDN — sab network par hi chalta hai. Interview ka "what is a network" ka yahi foundation answer hai.

Internet sirf "networks ka network" hai — ek single monolithic system nahi.
Har hop par packet ko naya framing ya routing milta hai — do packets ka path change ho sakta hai.

lessons.name: Network Devices — hubs, switches, routers, and what they do
lessons.desc: Hub broadcasts data to all devices (dumb). Switch sends data only to the target device (smart, uses MAC address). Router connects different networks together (uses IP address). Modem converts digital to analog.
lessons.q: What are the different types of network devices and what does each do? When would you use a switch vs a router?
lessons.qsub: What layer does a switch operate at vs a router? What is the difference between Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking?
terms: Simple device — data ko har port par broadcast karta hai.
MAC address dekhta hai — data sirf sahi device ko bhejta hai.
Do alag networks ko jodta hai, IP routing karta hai.
Har device ka physical unique address (Layer-2).
lessons.what:
Different devices network mein alag-alag kaam karte hain. Hub sabse simple hai — jo data aata hai usse har port par broadcast kar deta hai. Switch zyada smart hai — MAC address dekhta hai aur data sirf sahi device ko bhejta hai. Router sabse smart hai — ye do alag networks ko jodta hai aur IP address ke hisaab se packet ko sahi route deta hai.

Hub = sabko batao, Switch = exact ko bhejo, Router = do networks ke beech ka pul jo routing table se rasta banata hai.
lessons.analogy: Hub sabse chauk (square) jaisa hai jahan awaaz sab jagah jaati hai. Switch seedha darwaza khol kar usi kamre mein jaata hai. Router bada trafik police hai jo har gaadi ko sahi highway par bhejta hai.
lessons.why: Har device apne layer par kaam karta hai: Hub/Switch Layer-2 (MAC), Router Layer-3 (IP routing). Interview mein "hub vs switch vs router" bohat common distinction puchhi jaati hai — in sabki granularity samajhna zaroori hai.

Do VLANs / cloud subnets ko connect karta hai.

cons: Switch floods jab MAC unknown ho
Router config kompleks ho sakta hai

Router ek ghar mein LAN switch bhi hota hai — sab ek device mein combine.
Switch bhi VLAN se L3 routing kar sakta hai (multilayer switch).

lessons.name: Types of Networks — LAN, WAN, MAN, PAN
lessons.desc: LAN: your home or office network — fast, private. MAN: city-wide network. WAN: crosses cities/countries — the internet is a WAN. PAN: personal area (Bluetooth between devices).
lessons.q: What are the different types of computer networks? How do they differ in scale, speed, and ownership?
lessons.qsub: Cloud VPCs and subnets map to LAN/WAN concepts. How does understanding these help you design cloud infrastructure?
terms: Personal Area Network — ek insaan ke devices, bluetooth.
Local Area Network — ek office/building ke andar.
Wide Area Network — deshon ke paar — internet.
lessons.what:
Networks size aur geography ke hisaab se categories mein aate hain. PAN — ek insaan ke devices, jaise phone aur bluetooth earphone. LAN — ek building/office ke andar, jaise wifi home. MAN — ek shahar ko cover karta hai. WAN — bahut bada, deshon ke paar, aur internet ek WAN hai.

Asani se yaad: PAN (khud), LAN (ghar), MAN (shahar), WAN (duniya). Distance badhta hai, latency aur complexity bhi badhti hai.
lessons.analogy: Chai ka order system — PAN = apne phone se apne bluetooth, LAN = ek cafe ke andar staff walkie-talkie, MAN = shahar ke do cafes mein courier, WAN = desh ke do shahron ke beech train. Distance badhta hai, delay aur coordination bhi.
lessons.why: Classification se pata chalta hai ki latency, bandwidth, cost kya expect karein. WAN par cross-region request slow hota hai isliye CDN/edge lagate hain. Interview mein LAN vs WAN, aur ye ki VPN ek WAN-based concept hai, common hota hai.

Do WAN sites ko secure tunnel se jodta hai.

lessons.name: IP Address — the unique address of every device on the internet
lessons.desc: An IP address is a unique numerical label assigned to every device on a network. IPv4: 4 numbers separated by dots — 32 bits, ~4 billion addresses. IPv6: 128 bits, virtually unlimited. A port identifies a specific process.
lessons.q: What is an IP address and what is the difference between IPv4 and IPv6? What role do ports play?
lessons.qsub: What are private IP ranges? How does NAT allow multiple devices to share a single public IP?
terms: Har device ka network address — ghar ka pata jaisa.
Device ke andar specific service — 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS.
lessons.what:
Har device ko network par ek IP address chahiye — jaise ghar ka pata. IPv4 32-bit hota hai, 4 octets mein (192.168.1.1), aur ~4.3 billion addresses — ye khatam ho chuke hain. IPv6 128-bit, hex mein (2001:db8::1), bahut bada address space.

Port ek device ke andar kisi specific service ka pata — jaise 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS), 22 (SSH). IP device dhondhta hai, port specific app ko. IP + port ko socket kehte hain jo ek unique connection banata hai.
lessons.analogy: Flat ka address = IP (building ka pata), flat number = port (kaun sa kamra). IP packet ko building tak bhejta hai, port usse sahi room tak pahunchata hai. IPv4 purana city layout hai, IPv6 nayi bhari city.
lessons.why: IP address routing ka basis hai, aur port services ko differentiate karta hai. Bina IP ke packets destination nahi pahunchte, bina port ke server nahi samajhta ki request kaun si app ke liye hai. Interview ka networking ka root — IP/port hamesha poochha jata hai.

cons: Port conflicts (2 services ek port par nahi)

IPv4 4 billions se khatam ho gaya — NAT aur IPv6 iska ilaaj hain.
Port range sirf 0-65535 hai, aur 0-1023 privileged hote hain.

lessons.name: Subnetting & CIDR — dividing networks into smaller pieces
lessons.desc: CIDR notation: 192.168.1.0/24 means the first 24 bits are the network, last 8 bits are for hosts → 256 addresses. /16 = 65,536 addresses. Subnetting divides a large network into smaller sub-networks for security.
lessons.q: Explain CIDR notation. What does /24 mean and how many usable IP addresses does it provide?
lessons.qsub: How do you use CIDR notation when designing VPCs? What is a subnet mask and how does it work?
terms: IP space ko chhote networks mein baantna.
Pehle 24 bits network ka hissa, baaki host bits.
lessons.what:
Subnetting ek IP address space ko chhote networks mein baantne ka kaam hai. CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) notation IP ke saath prefix length likhta hai — jaise 192.168.1.0/24. /24 matlab pehle 24 bits network ke liye, baaki 8 bits hosts ke liye, yani 256 addresses (254 usable).

/32 = single address, /24 = 256, /16 = 65536. Ye prefix hi decide karta hai ki kaunsa part "network id" hai aur kaunsa "host id". Network + host bits se hi baaki address space banta hai.
lessons.analogy: Building ka lift system — ek puri building (IP space) ko floors (subnets) mein baato. Har floor ka apna wing (sub-subnet). CIDR ek shorthand hai — "floor /16 se /20" kehne jaisa. Compact aur scalable address division.
lessons.why: Subnetting se routing efficient hoti hai — bina /24 ke har IP ka alag route banana padta. Cloud mein VPC ke andar subnets CIDR se bante hain. Interview mein IP range calculate karna (usable hosts, block size) common hai.

IP range ka first + last address assign nahi hota (network + broadcast).
CIDR calculation mein host bits se 2 minus karna tha — common choote confusion ka ilaaj.

lessons.name: OSI Model & TCP/IP Stack — layers, encapsulation, PDUs
lessons.desc: OSI has 7 layers (Physical → Application). TCP/IP has 4 (Link → Internet → Transport → Application). Data is encapsulated as it moves down: data → segment → packet → frame → bits.
lessons.q: Explain the OSI model and the TCP/IP stack. How do they compare and why is understanding layers important?
lessons.qsub: What is encapsulation? Walk through what happens to HTTP data as it moves down the TCP/IP stack. What is each PDU called at each layer?
terms: 7 layers mein networking samjhane ka theoretical model.
Practical 4/5 layer model jo internet use karta hai.
Har layer data par apna header pahanta hai.
Protocol Data Unit — har layer ka data unit (segment/packet/frame).
lessons.what:
OSI model 7 layers mein networking ko samjhata hai: 1 Physical, 2 Data Link, 3 Network, 4 Transport, 5 Session, 6 Presentation, 7 Application. TCP/IP stack isko compact karta hai: Link, Internet, Transport, Application.

Encapsulation — data har layer par apna header pahanta hai (envelope ke andar envelope). PDU har layer ka data unit: Layer-4 = segment, L3 = packet, L2 = frame, L1 = bits. Har layer apne upar wale layer ko transparent treat karta hai. Receiver ulta kholta hai (de-encapsulation).
lessons.analogy: Gift packaging — andar gift (data), card (L7), envelope (L4), postage address (L3), truck label (L2), road (L1). Har layer ne apna label lagaya aur receiver ulta kholta hai (de-encapsulation). Ye stack ka core idea hai.
lessons.why: Layers se modularity — aap TCP ko HTTP ke saath bhi, UDP ke saath bhi use karte ho. Switch layer 2, router layer 3, load balancer L4/L7. Interview ke liye 7 layers ka naam + encapsulation story pakki rakhni chahiye.

lessons.name: TCP Deep Dive — handshake, congestion control, flow control
lessons.desc: TCP provides reliable, in-order delivery. 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK). Congestion control via slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit. Flow control via sliding window.
lessons.q: Explain the TCP 3-way handshake. How does TCP ensure reliable delivery and prevent congestion?
lessons.qsub: Describe TCP congestion control — slow start, congestion avoidance, and fast retransmit. Compare TCP variants like Cubic and BBR.
terms: Receiver ki buffer capacity — window size.
Network ki capacity — cwnd, slow start.
Data order track karne ke liye.
lessons.what:
TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) ek reliable, ordered, connection-oriented protocol hai. Connection banane ke liye 3-way handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK. Har segment ka acknowledgement hota hai, aur ordering ke liye sequence numbers use hote hain.

Do flow controls hain: Flow control receiver ki buffer capacity (window size) manage karta hai, aur congestion control network ki capacity (slow start, congestion avoidance) — taaki network overload na ho aur receiver buffer overflow na ho.
lessons.analogy: Video call mein "hello? hello?" — SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK se confirm hota hai ki dono baat kar rahe hain. Har baar receiver "haan mila" (ACK) karta hai; agar nahi mila, sender dubara bhejta hai. Slow start = dheere dheere speed badhao jab tak network bardasht kare.
lessons.why: TCP reliable delivery ka backbone hai — HTTP, databases, file transfer sab TCP par chalta hai. Connection setup, congestion window (cwnd), retransmission — inki samajh se interview ke network + distributed questions strong hote hain. HTTP/2 aur HTTPS dono TCP par hain.

SYN flood attack bina ACK wale handshake ka fayda uthata hai (half-open connections).

lessons.name: UDP — characteristics, use cases, vs TCP
lessons.desc: UDP is connectionless, unreliable, unordered. No handshake, no retransmission, no congestion control. Used where speed and low latency matter more than reliability.
lessons.q: What is UDP and how does it differ from TCP? When would you choose UDP over TCP?
lessons.qsub: Why is QUIC built on UDP instead of TCP? What advantages does this provide for HTTP/3?
terms: UDP ka data unit — fast, no acknowledgment.
Koi handshake/state nahi — fire and forget.
Packet drop ho sakta hai, pata nahi chalta.
lessons.what:
UDP (User Datagram Protocol) ek connectionless, unreliable, fast protocol hai. Koi 3-way handshake nahi, koi ACK nahi, koi ordering guarantee nahi. Aap bas data (datagram) bhej dete ho aur agar koi packet gir jaye to koi pata nahi chalta.

Ye low latency aur real-time use cases ke liye perfect hai: video calls, live gaming, DNS, VoIP. In cases mein agar ek frame gir jaye to usse replay karna irrelevant hota hai — aage badho, freshness zaroori hai.
lessons.analogy: Voice note (TCP) vs live call (UDP) — voice note mein har thought pura pahunchna chahiye (retry). Live call mein agar koi word gir gaya to aage badho, pichle ka intezaar mat karo. Live experience flexibility chahta hai, reliability nahi.
lessons.why: UDP ka fayda speed — no handshake, no ACK overhead, chhota header. Real-time apps UDP use karte hain. Interview mein TCP vs UDP comparison classic hai — trade-off samjhana zaroori hai.

UDP garantees: delivery nahi, ordering nahi, but speed hoti hai.
HTTP/3 ka QUIC UDP par chalta hai par usme TCP jaise reliability udhar (UDT) se milti hai.

lessons.name: DNS — resolution, record types, caching, CDN interplay
lessons.desc: DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses. Hierarchy: root → TLD (.com) → authoritative. Record types: A (IPv4), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME, MX, NS. Recursive vs iterative resolution.
lessons.q: How does DNS resolution work? Walk through what happens when you type a URL into a browser.
lessons.qsub: What are the key DNS record types and their purposes? How does TTL affect caching and DNS propagation?
terms: Root, TLD, Authoritative servers — lookup hierarchy.
A = IPv4 record, AAAA = IPv6 record.
Cache time-to-live — kitni der lookup yaad rahe.
lessons.what:
DNS (Domain Name System) domain name (google.com) ko IP address mein convert karta hai. Browser pehle DNS se IP puchhta hai, phir us IP par request bhejta hai.

Resolver tree: Root servers — TLD servers (.com) — Authoritative name servers. Record types: A (IPv4), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME (alias), MX (mail), TXT. Caching browser + resolver level par hota hai — TTL decide karti hai kitni der cache. CDN DNS ko geolocation-aware bana kar user ko nearest edge par bhejta hai.
lessons.analogy: Phone contact book — "Rohan" (name) dhondh kar uska number (IP) milta hai. Agar number change ho jaye to sirf contact book badlo. DNS yahi karta hai — naam se pata. TTL = kitna der number (IP) haath mein yaad rakhna hai.
lessons.why: DNS ke bina hum IP yaad nahi rakh sakte. CDN DNS geolocation se requests optimize karta hai. DNS har web request ka pehla step hai — latency, caching aur record types ka gyaan zaroori hai.

lessons.name: HTTP/1.1 — request/response model, keep-alive, pipelining
lessons.desc: HTTP/1.1: text-based, request-response over TCP. Keep-alive reuses connection for multiple requests. Pipelining sends next request before previous response arrives (never worked well).
lessons.q: How does HTTP/1.1 work? What was the motivation for creating HTTP/2?
lessons.qsub: What is HOL (Head-of-Line) blocking in HTTP/1.1? How did pipelining attempt to solve it and why did it fail?
terms: Client method+URI bhejta hai, server status+body deta hai.
Ek TCP connection par multiple requests (persistent).
Multiple requests bina intezaar, par responses order mein.
Slow first response baaki responses ko block karta hai.
lessons.what:
HTTP/1.1 web ka sabse zyada use hone wala version hai. Ek request-response cycle: client request bhejta hai (method + uri + headers), server response (status + headers + body). Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH.

Shuru mein har request ke liye naya TCP connection hota tha — slow. HTTP/1.1 ne keep-alive (persistent connection par multiple requests) aur pipelining (bina intezaar multiple requests ek saath, par responses order mein — isi se HOL blocking) add kiya. Response size Content-Length ya Transfer-Encoding: chunked se identify hota hai.
lessons.analogy: Grocery counter — pehle har item ke liye nayi line (connection) — slow. Keep-alive = ek hi counter par saare items ek baar mein, ek ke baad ek. Pipelining = poora order ek saath do, par jab tak pehla item ready nahi, baaki nahi — isi ko HOL blocking kehte hain.
lessons.why: HTTP/1.1 ek important baseline hai — request/response model samjhe bina HTTP/2/3 ka difference nahi banega. Interview ka "how does HTTP work" ka seedha answer isi par hai. Methods, status codes zaroori hain.

lessons.name: HTTP/2 — multiplexing, binary framing, HPACK, server push
lessons.desc: HTTP/2 is binary, multiplexed: multiple streams over one TCP connection. HPACK compresses headers. Server push sends resources before the client asks.
lessons.q: What are the key features of HTTP/2? How does binary framing improve performance over HTTP/1.1?
lessons.qsub: What is HPACK and how does it compress HTTP headers? What limitation does HTTP/2 still have that HTTP/3 solves?
terms: Ek TCP connection par parallel requests/responses.
Headers/body binary frames mein, streams ke andar.
Server client ke poochne se pehle resources bhej sakta hai.
lessons.what:
HTTP/2 HTTP/1.1 ki problems solve karne ke liye aaya. Key features: multiplexing (ek connection par parallel streams), binary framing (data binary frames mein, streams ke through), HPACK (header compression), aur server push (server proactively resources bhejta hai).

Har request ab ek stream hai, aur ek connection par kayi streams parallel chal sakte hain — isse connection-level HOL blocking solve ho gaya. Par note: TCP ke andar ab bhi logical HOL reh sakta hai (ek packet loss poore connection ko rokta hai). HTTP/2 bhi TCP ke upar hi hai.
lessons.analogy: Highway ek lane vs kayi lanes — HTTP/1.1 ek lane, gaddiyan ek ke peeche ek (HOL). HTTP/2 ek hi toll (single connection) par kayi lanes (streams) — requests parallel. HPACK = har gaadi apna pura bir card na le, ek common bir card folder.
lessons.why: Web apps ko bahut saare resources (CSS, JS, images) chahiye. HTTP/1.1 mein parallel ke liye 6+ connections lagte the. HTTP/2 ek connection par sab kuch — lower latency + better utilization. Browsers, Nginx, CDN sab HTTP/2 support karte hain.

HTTP/2 practically abhi TLS ke under hi chalta hai (h2 over TLS).
Ghost: multiplexing HOL ko connection-level mein khatam karta hai, par packet-level HOL abhi bhi TCP da deta hai.

lessons.name: HTTP/3 & QUIC — 0-RTT, connection migration, built-in encryption
lessons.desc: HTTP/3 runs over QUIC (UDP), not TCP. QUIC provides: 0-RTT handshake, connection migration (change networks without reconnect), built-in TLS 1.3, multiplexing without HOL blocking.
lessons.q: What is HTTP/3 and how does QUIC improve upon HTTP/2? What problems does running over UDP solve?
lessons.qsub: How does 0-RTT work in QUIC? What is connection migration and why is it critical for mobile users?
terms: Google ka UDP-based transport — TCP+TLS integrated.
Cached session se pehle data bhejna, bina extra handshake.
IP badle par connection jinda (connection ID).
Har stream independent — ek ka loss doosri ko block nahi.
lessons.what:
HTTP/3 aur QUIC transport ko UDP par le gaye. QUIC ek transport protocol hai jo TCP + TLS + HTTP ko combine karta hai aur UDP ke upar chalta hai. Isse 0-RTT connection establish hota hai — cached session se data pehla packet ke saath hi bheja ja sakta hai.

Sabse bada feature: connection migration — wifi se mobile data par switch karo, IP badalta hai, par QUIC connection jinda rehta hai (connection ID se). Har stream independent hai, isliye ek stream ka packet loss doosri ko block nahi karta — no HOL blocking.
lessons.analogy: VIP gate pass — TCP ke har naye visit ke liye firse queue (handshake). QUIC VIP card hai jo watermark wali gate se turant pass (0-RTT). Agar hotel (network) badlo, VIP card (connection ID) ke saath wahi room use karoge — migration!
lessons.why: Mobile networks mein IP constantly badalta hai, aur TCP/HTTP/2 wahan ruk jati hai. QUIC migration + 0-RTT + independent streams = poor mobile users ke liye smooth. Google, Meta, Cloudflare mass-scale HTTP/3 use karte hain.

lessons.name: HTTPS & TLS — handshake, cipher suites, certificate chain, ALPN
lessons.desc: TLS 1.3 handshake: ClientHello → ServerHello + certificate + finished → client finished. Cipher suites define key exchange + auth + cipher + MAC. Certificate chain validates trust.
lessons.q: How does a TLS 1.3 handshake work? What is the difference between TLS 1.2 and 1.3?
lessons.qsub: What is a certificate chain and how does the browser validate it? What is ALPN and why is it important?
terms: Cipher neg + cert verify + shared key exchange.
lessons.what:
HTTPS = HTTP + TLS (Transport Layer Security). TLS handshake: client aur server cipher suites negotiate karte hain, server apna certificate dikhata hai, client use verify karta hai, phir shared session key exchange hota hai (RSA ya ECDHE), aur uske baad data encrypted hota hai.

Certificate chain: Root CA → Intermediate CA → Server cert. Browser root CA par trust karta hai, isliye server cert verify hota hai. Cipher suite decide karta hai kaunsi algorithms hongi (jaise TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256).
lessons.analogy: Locked diary with seal — TLS handshake pehle ek secure line banata hai: server "meri identity ye seal (cert) se verify karo, aur ye lock (cipher) exchange do". Uske baad diary (data) locked jaata hai aur sirf dono ke paas key hai. Pehle uss key par trust (chain) check hota hai.
lessons.why: Bina HTTPS ke har packet wire par padha ja sakta hai (MITM). HTTPS data confidentiality + integrity + authentication deta hai. Interview ka "how does TLS work" + certificate chain + cipher suites samajhna zaroori hai.

lessons.name: WebSocket & SSE — upgrade handshake, full-duplex, event streams
lessons.desc: WebSocket is bidirectional, full-duplex over a single TCP connection after HTTP upgrade. SSE (Server-Sent Events) is unidirectional server→client text/event-stream. Both enable real-time communication.
lessons.q: How does WebSocket work? Compare WebSocket vs SSE — when would you use each?
lessons.qsub: How do you scale WebSocket connections across multiple servers? Why are sticky sessions or external pub/sub needed?
terms: Client + server dono messages bhejte hain.
Server-Sent Events — sirf server to client stream.
WebSocket messages binary/text frames ke through.
lessons.what:
WebSocket aur SSE (Server-Sent Events) real-time communication ke liye hain. WebSocket ek full-duplex channel hai — client aur server dono message bhej sakte hain. Ek upgrade handshake (HTTP GET with Upgrade: websocket) se HTTP → persistent WebSocket connection ban jata hai, phir low-overhead frames par data flow hota hai.

SSE sirf server-to-client one-way stream hai (text/event-stream). WebSocket chats/real-time games ke liye, SSE notification feeds ya streaming updates ke liye (jo sirf server se aana hai).
lessons.analogy: Walkie-talkie vs radio broadcast — WebSocket walkie-talkie jaisa full-duplex: dono side baat karte hain. SSE sirf radio broadcast: ek direction (server se client). Agar sirf server se updates aane hain (notification), SSE simpler + lighter hai.
lessons.why: Classic HTTP mein client ko poochhna padta hai (polling). Real-time apps (chat, notifications, dashboards) ke liye server ko pehal karni chahiye. WebSocket/SSE se low-latency push possible — koi live app iske bina nahi chalta.

lessons.name: gRPC & Protocol Buffers — HTTP/2-based, streaming, code generation
lessons.desc: gRPC uses HTTP/2 for transport and Protocol Buffers for serialization. Supports unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, bidirectional streaming. Auto-generates client/server stubs.
lessons.q: What is gRPC and how does it compare to REST? What are the advantages of Protocol Buffers over JSON?
lessons.qsub: What streaming patterns does gRPC support? How does deadline propagation work in gRPC calls?
terms: Google ka efficient binary serialization format.
Service + message types define karne wali schema.
lessons.what:
gRPC ek modern RPC framework hai jo HTTP/2 ke upar chalta hai aur Protocol Buffers (protobuf) serialization ke liye use karta hai. Aap ek .proto file mein service + message types define karte ho, aur compiler (protoc) se typed client/server code generate hota hai.

4 types of RPC: unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, bidirectional-streaming. HTTP/2 multiplexing ki wajah se multiple streaming calls ek connection par. Small binary payload + strong typing + codegen = microservices ke liye perfect.
lessons.analogy: Order form with fixed fields — REST jaise free-form email (JSON, flexible), gRPC jaise printed order form (protobuf, structured, efficient). Ek baar form (proto) define karke printing (codegen) automatic — har language mein typed version. Phir form chhota aur fast (binary) pahunchta hai.
lessons.why: Microservices ko ek dusre se baar-baar, structured, low-latency communication chahiye. JSON parsing slow + error-prone hai. gRPC binary + streaming + codegen se service-to-service call fast aur safe hota hai — Google internally isi se chalta hai.

lessons.name: L4 vs L7 Load Balancing — algorithms, health checks, session persistence
lessons.desc: L4 LB routes by IP:port (TCP/UDP), fast, no header inspection. L7 LB inspects HTTP headers, paths, cookies — slower but smarter. Algorithms: round-robin, least connections, IP hash.
lessons.q: What is the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing? When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: What load balancing algorithms are commonly used? How do health checks work at L4 vs L7?
terms: Traffic ko multiple servers par baantne wala.
Layer 4 — IP + port dekhta hai, fast, opaque.
Layer 7 — HTTP URL/headers dekhkar smart routing.
User ko hamesha same backend par bhejna.
lessons.what:
Load balancing incoming traffic ko multiple servers par bantta hai taaki koi server overload na ho. L4 (Layer 4) balancer sirf IP + port dekhta hai — fast, opaque forward. L7 (Layer 7) balancer HTTP layer par kaam karta hai — URL, headers, cookies dekhkar smart routing.

L4: fast, but no smart routing. L7: path/host based routing, TLS, caching — but more CPU. Nginx, HAProxy, AWS ALB = L7; AWS NLB, k8s kube-proxy = L4.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant manager — L4 sirf "kitne log aaye" (IP:port) count karke counter assign karta hai, order nahi dekhta. L7 manager order dekhta hai (URL: "/pizza", "/healthy") aur sahi kitchen (server) ko bhejta hai. L7 smarter, lekin slow.
lessons.why: Capability ke hisaab se: URL-based routing, sticky sessions, TLS termination chahiye to L7; raw TCP/UDP fast forwarding chahiye to L4. Interview mein "why L4 vs L7" classic hai.

lessons.name: Reverse Proxy — Nginx, Envoy, HAProxy — configuration patterns
lessons.desc: Reverse proxy sits in front of backend servers. Provides: TLS termination, caching, compression, rate limiting, request routing, canary deployments.
lessons.q: What is a reverse proxy and what are its common use cases? Compare Nginx, Envoy, and HAProxy.
lessons.qsub: How would you configure Nginx as a reverse proxy? What is the purpose of proxy_set_header directives?
terms: Client aur backend ke beech ka gateway.
Proxy HTTPS dekhta hai, backend HTTP.
Client ke liye internet access karne wala.
lessons.what:
Reverse proxy client aur backend ke beech ek gateway hai — client proxy se baat karta hai, proxy backend se. Ye Nginx, Envoy, HAProxy jaise tools hain. Kaam: load balance, TLS termination, caching, gzip, request modification, aur backend ko client se chhupana.

Forward proxy client ke liye hota hai (internet access), reverse proxy server ke aage hota hai (incoming traffic). Reverse proxy static files bhi serve kar sakta hai, rate limit, circuit breaker sab sambhalta hai.
lessons.analogy: Security guard at building gate — saare visitors (clients) guard (reverse proxy) se milte hain, guard unhe sahi floor (backend service) par bhejta hai. Visitors ko pata nahi floor ka actual arrangement (backends hidden). Guard uniformed (TLS), bag check (auth), crowd control (rate limit).
lessons.why: Ek hi entry point se aap control karte ho: security, TLS, caching, routing, gzip sab ek jagah. Backend simple rehta hai. Production har system ke aage ek reverse proxy (Nginx/Envoy) hota hai.

lessons.name: API Gateway — routing, auth, rate limiting, aggregation
lessons.desc: API Gateway is a specialized L7 proxy for APIs. Handles: request routing, authentication, rate limiting, caching, response aggregation, API versioning, billing.
lessons.q: What is an API Gateway and what problems does it solve? How does it differ from a reverse proxy?
lessons.qsub: How does an API Gateway handle authentication and rate limiting? What is request aggregation and when would you use it?
terms: Single entry point for all backend APIs.
lessons.what:
API Gateway ek single entry point hai jo client ke liye saare backend APIs expose karta hai. Ye reverse proxy + extra features: routing (path→service), authentication (JWT/OAuth check), rate limiting (per-client quota), aur aggregation (multiple service calls ka ek response — BFF pattern).

Also: protocol translation, transformation, caching, monitoring. Examples: Kong, AWS API Gateway, Nginx. Gateway client se backend orchestration chhupata hai.
lessons.analogy: Airport main desk — saara check-in (auth), security (validation), baggage (rate limit), flight assignment (routing) ek jagah. Agar 3 services ka data chahiye, desk sab call karke ek packet deta hai (aggregation). Bina desk ke har traveller khud saare counters par jata.
lessons.why: Microservices mein client ko har service ka URL + auth + rate-limit pata rakhna mushkil hai. Gateway sab centrally manage karta hai: ek API key, ek URL, sab policies ek jagah. Security + DX dono improve.

lessons.name: CDN — edge caching, origin shield, DDoS protection
lessons.desc: CDN caches content at edge servers close to users. Origin shield is a single intermediary cache that shields the origin from edge misses. CDNs absorb DDoS traffic at the edge.
lessons.q: How does a CDN work? What is the difference between edge caching and origin shield?
lessons.qsub: How do CDNs handle cache invalidation? What role do CDNs play in DDoS protection?
terms: User ke paas ka CDN server.
lessons.what:
CDN (Content Delivery Network) static content (images, CSS, JS, video) ko duniya bhar ke edge servers par cache karta hai, taaki user ko nearest server se content mile (low latency). DNS request ko user location ke hisaab se nearest edge par route karta hai.

Key concepts: edge caching, origin shield (edge→shield→origin jo origin traffic kam karta hai), aur DDoS protection (traffic absorb karke origin ko bachana). Cache invalidation purge aur Cache-Control headers se hoti hai.
lessons.analogy: Local chai stall vs central tea factory — har mohalle mein stalls (edge) copies rakhkar serve karte hain, factory (origin) ko har baar nahi bulaya jata. Kisi ko speed milti hai (latency). Bada rush ho to stalls (CDN) sambhalte hain aur factory (origin) safe rahta hai.
lessons.why: Network latency distance ke saath badhti hai (RTT). CDN content ko user ke paas laata hai — page load, video streaming aur worldwide users ki experience behtar. Bina CDN ke cross-region slow + origin overloaded.

lessons.name: Service Mesh — sidecar proxy, mTLS, traffic splitting
lessons.desc: Service mesh is a dedicated infrastructure layer for service-to-service communication. Sidecar proxy (Envoy) injected alongside each service. Provides mTLS, traffic splitting, circuit breaking.
lessons.q: What is a service mesh? How does a sidecar proxy work? Compare Istio and Linkerd.
lessons.qsub: How does a service mesh enable mTLS and traffic splitting for canary deployments? What is circuit breaking?
terms: Microservices traffic manage karne wala infrastructure layer.
Har service ke paas Envoy jaise proxy.
lessons.what:
Service mesh microservices ke beech ka saara network traffic manage karta hai. Har service ke saath ek sidecar proxy (jaise Envoy) judta hai jo traffic intercept karta hai — bina application code badle. Features: mTLS, traffic splitting (canary/blue-green), retries, timeouts, tracing, observability.

Architecture: control plane (config + cert management) aur data plane (sidecars). Popular: Istio (Envoy), Linkerd, Consul Connect.
lessons.analogy: Couriers har service ke bahar — service mesh har service ke paas ek courier (sidecar) rakhta hai jo saara traffic sambhalta hai. App sirf apna kaam karta hai; courier security (mTLS), routing (traffic split), retry sab sambhalta hai. Boss (control plane) couriers ko naye rules bhejta hai.
lessons.why: Microservices mein retry/mTLS/tracing har jagah application code mein dalna mushkil hai. Service mesh ise infrastructure layer par shift karke app simple rakhta hai — networking policies ek jagah. Interview important concept.

lessons.name: Firewalls & ACLs — stateful vs stateless, security groups, NACLs
lessons.desc: Stateless firewall examines each packet independently. Stateful tracks connection state, allows return traffic automatically. AWS Security Groups are stateful instance-level. NACLs are stateless subnet-level.
lessons.q: What is the difference between stateful and stateless firewalls? How does defense-in-depth work in cloud networking?
lessons.qsub: In AWS, what is the difference between Security Groups and Network ACLs? Why would you use both?
terms: Traffic ko rules se allow/deny karne wala.
Connection state track karta hai — replies auto-allow.
Har packet independent — both directions rules chahiye.
lessons.what:
Firewall network traffic ko rules ke hisaab se allow/deny karta hai. ACL (Access Control List) rule set hota hai — source, dest, port, allow/deny. Stateful firewall connection state track karta hai — ek baar connection allowed to uski return traffic automatically allowed.

Stateless firewall har packet ko independent treat karta hai — usse pata nahi ki packet return traffic hai ya naya request. Isliye har direction ke liye alag rules chahiye. Stateful = samajhdar (connection aware), Stateless = simple par rigid.
lessons.analogy: Building security — stateless guard: har visitor ko dobara identity dikhani padti hai, chahe woh 2 second pehle andar gaya ho. Stateful guard: aapka record hai, ek baar manzoor, phir session ke dauran free aana-jaana. Stateful ko reply traffic puri tarah samajh aa jata hai.
lessons.why: Security ka pehla line — external se sirf allowed ports (80, 443) khule rakna. Stateful complexity se replies/multipart samajhne mein aasani hoti hai. Interview mein stateful vs stateless firewall difference common hai.

lessons.name: DDoS Protection — volumetric, protocol, application-layer attacks
lessons.desc: Volumetric: UDP floods, amplification (DNS/NTP). Protocol: SYN flood, ping of death. Application-layer: slowloris, HTTP flood. Mitigation: rate limiting, CDN scrubbing, WAF.
lessons.q: What are the three types of DDoS attacks? How would you design a multi-layer DDoS mitigation strategy?
lessons.qsub: What is a SYN flood and how do SYN cookies mitigate it? What does AWS Shield Standard vs Advanced protect against?
terms: Distributed DoS — overwhelming traffic se takrana.
Legit requests se app resources overuse — HTTP flood.
lessons.what:
DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) system ko kaam karne se rokta hai — botnet se overwhelming traffic bhej kar. 3 types: volumetric (network bandwidth saturate — UDP flood), protocol (connection state exhaust karo — SYN flood), aur application-layer (legit-looking HTTP flood / slowloris — app resources overuse).

Protection: rate limiting, WAF (L7), CDN/scrubbing center, anycast (traffic multiple locations par), auto-scaling. App-layer attacks sabse tricky — woh legit traffic jaisa dikhta hai.
lessons.analogy: Shop par bhir — volumetric = gali ke sab log entries block karke khade (bandwidth saturation). Protocol = kharab tickets se guard ki queue bhar do (SYN queue full). App-layer = fake customers jo aage badh ke time le rahe hain (slow requests) — sabse chalak.
lessons.why: DDoS hone par availability impacted — business money lose karta hai. Interview mein categories + layered mitigation (edge absorb + rate-limit + autoscale) dikhao. CDN/scrubbing pehle se plan karna achi practice hai.

SYN flood mitigation: SYN cookies / proxy absorbing half-open connections.

lessons.name: Network Segmentation — VPC, subnets, private/public, NAT gateway
lessons.desc: VPC provides an isolated virtual network. Subnets segment within a VPC (public with internet gateway, private without). NAT Gateway enables outbound internet from private subnets.
lessons.q: How would you design a VPC network with public and private subnets? What is the purpose of a NAT Gateway?
lessons.qsub: What is VPC peering and when would you use Transit Gateway instead? How does network segmentation limit blast radius?
terms: Bade network ko chhote isolated parts mein baantna.
Virtual Private Cloud — isolated virtual network.
Private instances outbound internet, bina public IP.
lessons.what:
Network segmentation bade network ko chhote isolated parts mein baanta hai — jaise VPC ke andar subnets (public/private), har part ka apna security. VPC ek isolated virtual network hai. NAT gateway private subnet ke instances ko (bina public IP ke) internet se connect karne deta hai — outbound hai, inbound blocked.

Segmentation se risk kam: agar ek subnet compromise ho, baaki safe (lateral movement stop). Public subnet = internet-facing (web), private = database/backend (no public access).
lessons.analogy: Bank ka vault system — har compartment ka apna access. Lobby (public subnet) sabke liye khula, vault room (db subnet) sirf restricted staff. NAT gateway gated entrance hai jisse andar se bahar ja sakte ho (internet) par bahar se andar nahi bina permission.
lessons.why: Flat network mein koi bhi compromise poore network ka access de deta. Segmentation defense-in-depth ka core — sensitive data (DB) alag. Cloud security interviews mein VPC/subnet/NAT architecture pucha jata hai.

lessons.name: Zero Trust Networking — beyond VPC, mTLS, identity-based access
lessons.desc: Zero Trust: "never trust, always verify" — no implicit trust based on network location. Every request must be authenticated and authorized, regardless of origin.
lessons.q: What is Zero Trust networking? How does it differ from perimeter-based security?
lessons.qsub: How does mTLS work and why is it central to Zero Trust architectures? What is BeyondCorp and SPIFFE?
terms: Sirf zaroori access — kam se kam.
lessons.what:
Zero Trust Networking ka principle: "Never trust, always verify" — network ke andar hona means automatically trusted nahi. Har request ko authenticate + authorize karna hoga chahe source internal ho ya external.

Core: mTLS (dono sides encrypted + verify), identity-based access, micro-segmentation, continuous verification, least privilege. VPN/segmentation ka purana model "network access = trust" ko replace karta hai.
lessons.analogy: Hotel jahan har darwaza locked — normal: ek baar lobby (network) mein aa gaye to saare kamre khule. Zero trust: lobby mein bhi, har kamre (service) ki apni alag key (identity) chahiye, har baar verify. "Maine lobby se aaya" kaafi nahi.
lessons.why: Perimeter (firewall) toot gaya to attacker poore resources access karta hai. Zero trust se uske paas sirf us resource ka access jiska uski identity se tag hai — lateral movement rukti hai. mTLS + identity policies backbone hain.

lessons.name: VPN & Private Connectivity — IPsec, Direct Connect, VPC peering
lessons.desc: VPN creates an encrypted tunnel over the internet (IPsec, OpenVPN). Direct Connect is a private physical connection from on-prem to cloud. VPC peering/Transit Gateway connect VPCs within the cloud.
lessons.q: What are the options for connecting on-premises networks to the cloud? Compare VPN vs Direct Connect.
lessons.qsub: How does Transit Gateway simplify multi-VPC connectivity? What is a common HA pattern for hybrid connectivity?
terms: Internet ke upar encrypted site-to-site tunnel.
Dedicated private line on-premise to cloud (AWS).
Do VPCs ko direct private network se jorna.
lessons.what:
VPN aur private connectivity secure channel banate hain taaki do sites/services baat kar saken. IPsec VPN — internet ke upar encrypted tunnel (site-to-site). Direct Connect (AWS) — dedicated private line on-premise se AWS, bina public internet. VPC peering — do VPCs ko direct private network se jorna.

Choice: IPsec = cheap, internet-based, variable latency. Direct Connect = dedicated high-speed, stable, costly. Peering = same cloud, fast. Private connectivity se data public internet se nahi guzarta — security + consistency.
lessons.analogy: Railway vs regular road — VPN regular highway (internet) par overlay route, cheap, par traffic ke hisaab se latency varying. Direct Connect dedicated railway track — sirf aapki train, stable, par build karne ka kharcha. Peering = do buildings ke beech direct footbridge.
lessons.why: Production mein on-premise data center se cloud ko secure + stable chahiye. Public internet par latency change + risk. Direct Connect/IPsec private path — predictability + compliance. Hybrid cloud interview point.

lessons.name: Caching Strategies — client, server, CDN, cache invalidation
lessons.desc: Cache types: browser (HTTP cache), CDN (edge cache), server (Redis/Memcached), application (in-memory). Invalidation: TTL-based, write-through, write-behind, cache-aside.
lessons.q: What are the different types of caching in a web architecture? Explain cache-aside vs write-through patterns.
lessons.qsub: What is a cache stampede and how do you prevent it? What is stale-while-revalidate and when would you use it?
terms: App pehle cache, miss par DB + set cache.
lessons.what:
Caching baar-baar use hone wala data fast storage mein rakhna hai. Levels: client cache (browser), server cache (CDN/edge), application cache (Redis). Invalidation cache fresh rakhta hai — data change ho to cache hatao.

Strategies: cache-aside (read cache, miss par DB + set), write-through (har write cache+DB), TTL expiry, invalidation events. Headers Cache-Control, ETag freshness control karte hain.
lessons.analogy: Kitchen fridge vs market — fridge (cache) mein daily ka poshada, har baar market (DB) nahi jate. Kabhi koi item kharab ho jaye (stale), bahar nikaalo (invalidate), naya lao. Fridge bhara rahe to market se naye items ko refill karo (write-through).
lessons.why: Caching latency aur load kam karta hai. Read-heavy apps (news, product pages) ke liye lifeline — better performance, lower DB load, cheaper CDN. Interview ka "how do you cache" + TTL/invalidation balance classic hai.

lessons.name: Distributed Systems Networking — gossip protocols, consistent hashing
lessons.desc: Gossip protocol: nodes periodically exchange state with random peers — converges without central coordination. Consistent hashing maps keys to nodes with minimal reshuffling on topology changes.
lessons.q: How do gossip protocols work and where are they used? What problem does consistent hashing solve?
lessons.qsub: What are virtual nodes in consistent hashing? How do Cassandra and Redis Cluster use these protocols?
terms: Info nodes ke beech viral (eventually consistent).
Nodes par hash-ring se data distribution.
Uneven distribution se bachne ke liye.
Kaunse nodes upar hain — gossip se detect hota hai.
lessons.what:
Gossip protocol — information nodes ke beech viral tarah spread hoti hai: har node apni jaankari friends ko batata hai, chain reaction se sab jaante hain. Clusters mein membership, failure detection ke liye useful.

Consistent hashing — data nodes par baantne ka tarika jisse node add/remove hone par sirf kuch portion relocate hota hai. Har node ek hash ring par assigned; key ka hash nearest node ko jata hai. Cache/distributed store mein node churn cheap banati hai.
lessons.analogy: Gossip = office rumour — ek ne suna, do-do ko bataya, taiz gossip sab tak pahunchta hai (eventually consistent). Consistent hashing = taxi stand ke slots — har porter (node) ka fixed slot ring par; naya kaam (key) nearest slot. Jab ek porter chhut jaye (node down), sirf uske customers dusre slot par — baaki unaffected.
lessons.why: Clusters mein har node ka state sabko pata hona zaroori (gossip) — membership/failure detection reliable. Data balanced hona chahiye bina poor rebalance (consistent hashing) — scale out cheap.

lessons.name: Rate Limiting — token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding window
lessons.desc: Token bucket refills tokens at steady rate — burst up to bucket size. Leaky bucket processes at steady rate — excess queued/dropped. Sliding window counters over recent time window.
lessons.q: Compare token bucket, leaky bucket, and sliding window rate limiting algorithms. When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: How do you implement distributed rate limiting across multiple servers? What consistency tradeoffs exist?
terms: Tokens bucket mein, fixed rate refresh — burst allow.
Fixed rate output queue — smooth, no burst.
Distributed rate limiting ke liye Lua/atomic.
lessons.what:
Rate limiting kisi client ya service ke requests ki sankhya ko rokna hai. Algorithms: token bucket — bucket tokens se bhara, har request ek token consume, fixed rate par tokens refresh (+ burst allowed). leaky bucket — fixed rate output queue, smooth processing, no burst. sliding window — recent fixed time window mein exact count, precise aging.

Token bucket: bursty par capped average. Leaky: bilkul smooth. Sliding: most accurate (no boundary spikes). Distributed ke liye Redis + Lua counters common.
lessons.analogy: Ticket counter — token bucket: har minute 60 ticket (tokens) add ho rahe, aap ek sath 60 use kar sakte ho (burst) phir bekaar. Leaky: line fixed speed se nikalti hai — rush ho to bhi smooth. Sliding window: exact "last 60 seconds ke 60 requests" count — boundary ke beech bhi sahi.
lessons.why: Rate limit malicious floods (DDoS, scraper) aur accidental spikes ko control karta hai. Algo choice: burst (token), smooth (leaky), precise (sliding). Distributed production ke liye Redis required.

lessons.name: Backpressure & Flow Control — TCP, HTTP, reactive streams
lessons.desc: Backpressure prevents a fast producer from overwhelming a slow consumer. TCP flow control (receiver window). HTTP/2 flow control (per-stream WINDOW_UPDATE). Reactive Streams demand-based push.
lessons.q: What is backpressure and why is it critical in distributed systems? How do TCP and HTTP/2 implement flow control?
lessons.qsub: How do reactive streams handle backpressure? What happens in a message queue when the consumer can't keep up?
terms: Producer ko slow kar dena jab consumer overburdened.
Slow stream piche wale ko rokna.
lessons.what:
Backpressure & flow control system ko overrun hone se rokta hai jab producer consumer se fast ho. TCP window size se flow control karta hai — receiver buffer bharne par sender garso slow ho jata hai. HTTP/2 stream-level flow control frames deta hai. Reactive streams (RxJS, Project Reactor, Node streams) demand-based backpressure — consumer "kitna chahiye" batata hai, producer utna hi bhejta hai.

Apply: bina backpressure ke memory/buffer overflow — app crash. Isliye queues bounded rakho ya producer coordinate karo.
lessons.analogy: Ek gluten ka truck vs godown — agar godown (receiver) bhar chuka hai aur truck (sender) ghoomta hi raha to warehouse overflow. Deterministic backpressure: godown "abhi 5 boxes do" kehta hai — truck 5 bhejta hai, wait. TCP/Pipes exactly yahi demand-signal karte hain.
lessons.why: Bina flow control ke fast producer poor system ko memory/queue se overflow kar deta. TCP it's built-in (window). High-level apps (streaming, message queues) mein explicit backpressure pattern chahiye taaki stability. Interview "how do you handle backpressure" common hai.

lessons.name: Network Performance — latency, bandwidth, throughput, jitter
lessons.desc: Latency: time for a packet to travel (one-way or RTT). Bandwidth: max data rate (bits/sec). Throughput: actual achieved rate. Jitter: variance in latency.
lessons.q: Explain the four key network performance metrics. How do they interact and which one matters most for different applications?
lessons.qsub: What is the Bandwidth-Delay Product? How does TCP window size limit throughput? What tools measure each metric?
lessons.what:
Latency ek chhote packet ke round-trip ka time (ms). Bandwidth channel ki max capacity (bps). Throughput actual data jo safely transfer hota hai (with protocol overhead). Jitter latency ki variation — real-time apps (VoIP, gaming) ke liye killer.

Relation: latency × bandwidth = bandwidth-delay product (data in flight). Video streaming throughput, chat latency, VoIP jitter matter karta hai. Measure tools: ping (latency), iperf (throughput), traceroute (path).
lessons.analogy: Highway — latency = ghar se nikalne par pehla sign aane ka time, bandwidth = kitne lanes hain (max cars), throughput = actual cars jo guzri (traffic + toll lagate hue), jitter = kabhi 5min kabhi 20min — jagged. VoIP/Games badi hai jitter: kabhi delay badhta hai to odd.
lessons.why: Interview mein performance metrics ki understanding zaroori — kaunsa metric kis use case mein matter karta hai. Diagnose karne ke liye latency/throughput/jitter alag-alag impact dikhana = senior signal.

lessons.name: Cloud Networking — VPC design, multi-region, hybrid cloud
lessons.desc: Cloud VPC design: large CIDR (/16) with subnets per tier (public, private-app, private-data) across 3 AZs. Multi-region: active-active or active-passive. Hybrid: Direct Connect + VPN to on-prem.
lessons.q: How do you design a VPC for production workloads? What considerations drive CIDR ranges and subnet layout?
lessons.qsub: What is PrivateLink and how does it enable cross-VPC service access? What are the cost tradeoffs of different connectivity options?
terms: Subnets + route tables + gateways ka layout.
lessons.what:
Cloud networking — VPC design se shuru: public subnets (web), private subnets (app/db), NAT gw, route tables, NACL/SG. Multi-region — data ko multiple regions mein replicate karna (geo redundancy, low latency). Hybrid cloud — on-premise data center ko cloud se connect (Direct Connect/VPN).

Design principles: least-privilege, blast radius, HA (multi-AZ), low-latency via edge/CDN. Traffic flow: client → CDN/cloudfront → LB → app (multi-AZ) → DB (private, replicated).
lessons.analogy: Building multiple secure wings — VPC = poora campus (isolated), subnets = wings (public lobby / private office / vault), AZs = alag-alag buildings taaki ek girne par doosra chal (HA). Multi-region = do alag campuses alag cities (geo redundancy). Hybrid = campus + remote office secure line se juda.
lessons.why: Production cloud apps ko availability + security + performance chahiye. Multi-AZ/region se downtime avoid, VPC me isolation se security. Interview mein "design a network for this service" mein yahi blocks dikhana hota hai.

lessons.name: Network Observability — tracing, metrics, packet capture, eBPF
lessons.desc: Network observability includes flow logs (VPC Flow Logs), packet capture (tcpdump, Wireshark), distributed tracing (trace_id across services), eBPF (in-kernel programmable observation).
lessons.q: What tools and techniques do you use for network observability in production? How do you debug a network issue?
lessons.qsub: What is eBPF and how does it enable modern observability tools like Cilium and Pixie?
terms: Request ko services ke paar follow karna (span graph).
Kernel mein program — observability bina instrument.
lessons.what:
Network observability — samjho ki network kya kar raha hai. Tracing (Jaeger/Zipkin) ek request ko multiple services ke paar follow karta hai (spans). Metrics (Prometheus) counters — latency, QPS, error rate. Packet capture (tcpdump/Wireshark) raw packets dekhna — retries, drops, retransmissions. eBPF kernel-internal program jo bina application code ke traffic observe karta hai.

Signal-to-noise: tracing=multi-service aware, metrics=aggregate numbers, packet capture=deepest raw. eBPF (Cilium, eBPF-based probes) = visibility with low overhead.
lessons.analogy: Journey tracking — metrics = GPS par "kitne km/hour" (avg). Tracing = har chauraha (service) ka log "kis route se gaya". Packet capture = har tyre ka dashcam video (raw). eBPF = car mein built-in sensor jo bina koi dash cam lagaye sab record karta hai — kernel level magic.
lessons.why: Network fail hota hai — retry storms, high latency, packet loss. Observability se pata chalta hai ki bottleneck kahan hai. Pocket interview: tracing jaeger, metrics prometheus, deep-debug tcpdump/eBPF.

lessons.name: Kubernetes Networking — CNI, service mesh, ingress, network policies
lessons.desc: Pod networking: CNI plugins assign IPs and route traffic. Service: kube-proxy handles cluster IP via iptables/IPVS. Ingress: L7 routing. NetworkPolicy: pod-level firewall.
lessons.q: How does networking work in Kubernetes? Explain the roles of CNI, kube-proxy, and Ingress.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between iptables and IPVS modes in kube-proxy? How does Cilium use eBPF for improved networking?
terms: Container Network Interface — pod networking plugin.
Pods ka stable virtual IP + DNS.
Cluster ke andar HTTP L7 routing.
Service IP -> pod IP forwarding rules.
lessons.what:
Kubernetes networking — pods ko ek flat network milta hai (har pod apna IP). CNI (Calico, Cilium) pod-to-pod networking + policies provide karta hai. Service pods ka stable virtual IP + DNS — pod churn se IP badalta hai par service constant. Ingress cluster ke andar se HTTP/L7 routing (path→service). kube-proxy service IP ko actual pod IP par forward karta hai.

External traffic: Ingress/LoadBalancer → Service → Pods. Network policies (CNI) pod-level micro-segmentation dete hain.
lessons.analogy: Apartment ka mail system — har kothri (pod) ka apna blank pata (IP). Society ka reception (Service) ek fixed address hai jo sab kothriyon tak pahunchata hai — kothri badal jaye (pod restarted) to reception wahi rahega. Security guard (network policy) decide karta hai kaunsi kothri kisi se baat kar sakti hai.
lessons.why: Kubernetes networking interview + real-world core hai. Pod IPs dynamic hain — Service abstraction zaroori. CNI + Ingress + policies samajh ke distributed deploy aasani se ho pata hai.

lessons.name: Network Resiliency — retry, circuit breaker, timeout, bulkhead
lessons.desc: Retry: resend on transient failures (with backoff). Circuit breaker: fail fast when downstream is unhealthy. Timeout: bound wait time. Bulkhead: isolate connection pools per dependency.
lessons.q: What are the four essential network resiliency patterns? How do retry and circuit breaker interact?
lessons.qsub: Why is jitter important in retry backoff? What is the thundering herd problem and how do you prevent it?
terms: Fail par request dobara — idempotency required.
Fail repeatedly par circuit open (fast fail).
Kitna der wait karna; deadline boundary.
Resources partition — ek failure doosre ko na rokaye.
lessons.what:
Network resiliency failures ko handle karta hai: retries (transient fail par dobara, bina blast radius), circuit breaker (repeated failure par circuit open — fast fail, bina wait), timeouts (deadline boundary — kitna der wait), aur bulkhead (resources ko partition karo — ek pool down ho to doosra na faste).

Patterns combine: timeout then retry with backoff then circuit opens vài bulkhead isolates. Jittered backoff + retry budget = sabotage nahi.
lessons.analogy: Customer service lines — retry = dobara dial karna thodi der baad (backoff). Circuit breaker = jab machine har baar busy, operator bole "abhi koi call mat lo, thoda ruko" (fast fail). Timeout = "5 min telefon mat lagao, band karo". Bulkhead = alag-alag kiosks taaki ek kiosk line fail ho to doosri continue.
lessons.why: Networks fail hota hai — transient blips, cascading failures. In patterns ke bina ek failure poore system ko gira deta (retry storm, timeout exhaustion). Interview mein "how do you make this resilient" ka answer yahi patterns hain.

lessons.name: BGP — Border Gateway Protocol, AS routing, route propagation
lessons.desc: BGP is the routing protocol of the internet. Autonomous Systems (AS) exchange routes via BGP. eBGP between ASes, iBGP within an AS. BGP selects routes based on AS-path length, local preference, MED. Route propagation is incremental — not periodic like OSPF.
lessons.q: What is BGP and how does it differ from OSPF? Why is BGP called a path vector protocol?
lessons.qsub: What is route hijacking and how does BGP prevent it? What is the difference between eBGP and iBGP?
terms: Autonomous System — ek org ka network block.
eBGP between ASes, iBGP within AS.
Route ka hop list — loop prevention.
lessons.what:
BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) internet ka routing protocol hai — different Autonomous Systems (AS) ke beech paise wale routers ko routes announce/choose karta hai. eBGP ASes ke bare mein, iBGP one AS ke andar. Har route ek prefix (CIDR) announce karta hai.

AS path route ki trustworthy-ness decide karta hai: chhota AS path = shorter route preferred. BGP path selection: weight, local-pref, AS path length, MED, then IGP metric. Cloud providers (AWS, GCP) BGP use karte hain (Direct Connect, VPN, cloud routers).
lessons.analogy: Highways between states — every state (AS) apne highways (routes) announce karta hai "meri taraf se 10.0.0.0/8 ja sakta hai". Drivers (routers) choose up shortest/easiest route (path). Agar ek rasta band (route withdrawn), BGP automatically alternative find. AS path = "kitne states cross karna hoga".
lessons.why: BGP internet ka glue hai — provider multi-homing, cloud hybrid, anycast CDN sab BGP se. Virtual Route table: "prefix + next-hop" ko BGP karne ke liye path se selekt hota hai. Interview mein "how does the internet route" ka answer BGP hi hai.

lessons.name: Ethernet — frames, MAC addresses, ARP, VLANs, switching
lessons.desc: Ethernet frames: preamble, destination MAC, source MAC, type, payload, FCS. MAC addresses are 48-bit hardware addresses. ARP resolves IP→MAC. VLANs (802.1Q tag) segment broadcast domains. Switches learn MACs by source address, flood unknown unicast.
lessons.q: What is the structure of an Ethernet frame? How does ARP resolve an IP to a MAC address?
lessons.qsub: What is a VLAN and how does it reduce broadcast traffic? How does a switch learn which port a MAC is on?
terms: Ek switch ko logical segments mein baantna (802.1Q).
L2 PDU: MAC hdr | payload | FCS.
lessons.what:
Ethernet Layer-2 LAN technology hai — devices ko MAC address se identify karta hai aur frames mein data bhejta hai. Switch MAC table se flooding instead of specific forwarding. ARP unknown IP ka MAC resolve karta hai (broadcast request). VLANs (802.1Q) ek switch ko logical isolated segments mein baant te hain — traffic segment hi rehta hai.

Frame: destination MAC, source MAC, EtherType, payload, FCS (checksum). MAC flooding / VLAN hopping — security attacks layer-2 par.
lessons.analogy: Building intercom (MAC) + delivery address — Ethernet = har flat ka physical intercom (MAC) jo switch (reception) se route hota hai. ARP = jab aapko pata na ho kis flat par janana hai, aap announce karte ho "202.54.1.5 konsa flat hai?" — wahi flat reply deta hai. VLAN = building ko floors mein alag-alag wings — har wing ka traffic isolated.
lessons.why: Layer-2 networking real LANs ka core hai — switches, MAC, ARP, VLANs har datacenter mein. Interview ke liye frame structure, switch learning, ARP resolution, VLAN isolation basics zaroori hain.

lessons.name: ICMP & Diagnostic Tools — ping, traceroute, path MTU discovery
lessons.desc: ICMP echoes (ping) test reachability and measure RTT. traceroute sends TTL=1,2,3... packets, receives ICMP time exceeded. Path MTU Discovery: send DF (Don't Fragment) bit, receive ICMP 'fragmentation needed' to find max MTU. Used for network diagnostics.
lessons.q: How does traceroute work? What is the difference between ping and traceroute?
lessons.qsub: How does Path MTU Discovery work? What is the problem with ICMP blackholes?
lessons.what:
ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) diagnostics ke liye hai — jaise ping (echo request/reply — host reachable hai aur RTT kya hai) aur traceroute (path ke har hop ka IP + latency). Path MTU discovery smallest MTU path par dhundta hai taaki packets fragment na hon.

ICMP types: echo (8), echo reply (0), destination unreachable (3), time exceeded (11). Uptime checks (ping), routing diagnosis (traceroute). ICMP can be rate-limited/blocked for security.
lessons.analogy: Postal status check — ping = "apna postcard bhejo, agar mile jab echo-reply, route + time pata ho". Traceroute = har post-office (hop) ki stamp — "kab tak pahuncha, kahan ruka". Path MTU = road ka sabse chhota bridge (MTU) — agar bada truck (packet) usse na guzre, use chhote (fragment) karo ya doosra rasta.
lessons.why: Network troubleshooting ka pehla tool ICMP hai — ping se reachability + RTT, traceroute se hop lag analyse. Interview mein "network slow hai, kaise diagnose karte ho" ka answer ICMP aata hai.

lessons.name: WiFi — 802.11 standards, association, encryption (WPA3)
lessons.desc: 802.11 defines WiFi. Standards: 802.11n (WiFi 4), 802.11ac (WiFi 5), 802.11ax (WiFi 6/6E). Association: scan → authenticate → associate. Encryption: WPA3 (SAE handshake, protected management frames). WPA2 vulnerable to KRACK attack. Channel contention via CSMA/CA.
lessons.q: What is the difference between WiFi 5 (802.11ac) and WiFi 6 (802.11ax)?
lessons.qsub: How does WPA3 improve on WPA2? What is CSMA/CA and how does it differ from Ethernet's CSMA/CD?
lessons.what:
WiFi IEEE 802.11 standard par chalta hai — versions: 802.11n (WiFi 4), ac (WiFi 5), ax (WiFi 6), be (WiFi 7). WPA3 latest security — SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals) dictionary attack resistant, forward secrecy. Bands: 2.4GHz (long range, congestion), 5GHz (faster, less range), 6GHz (newest, clean).

Security evolution: WEP (broken) → WPA → WPA2 → WPA3. SSID = network name, channel = frequency slice. WiFi is half-duplex (collision), uses CSMA/CA.
lessons.analogy: Radio walkie-talkie in a cafe — WiFi = wireless walkie-talkie lines (bands/channels) jis par devices baat karte hain. WPA3 = modern encryption lock jo guess-proof hai (SAE) — WEP/WPA purane kund Lane jab easily toote. 2.4GHz = lamba dora par bheed, 5GHz = fast par chhota area — trade-off.
lessons.why: WiFi interface + security topic interviews mein (system design for mobile, security basic) aa sakta hai. Backend developers ke liye kya-kya WPA versions, bands, CSMA/CA ka idea hona enough. Security WPA3 = modern standard.
